types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human being. Also called Individual, Human, Agent. Examples: Gianni Infantino, Patrice Motsepe, Aleksander Ceferin, FIFA president.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Person class directly matches the OIE_TYPE 'Person' and its definition, and all mentions are individual human beings.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose, such as a business, government department, or sports association. Also called Company, Institution, Association, Body, Federation. Examples: FIFA, Confederation of African Football, Football Association of Ireland, UEFA.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Organization class perfectly aligns with the OIE_TYPE 'Organization', its definition, and all provided examples of football governing bodies.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

types.embedding_query_text: Process: A series of actions or steps taken in order to achieve a particular end. Also called Procedure, Method, Operation, System. Examples: Elections, election, elections, re-election.

chosen_type.label: Election
chosen_type.definition: A formal process of making a decision or choosing a representative by voting.
chosen_type.justification: None of the candidate schema.org Action types fully capture 'Elections' as a broader process or event. Minting 'Election' as a specific type of Event is the best fit.

candidates.label: VoteAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a preference or choice from a predefined set of options. Also called casting a vote, ballot, election. Examples: voting in a political election, casting a vote for a competition winner, participating in a poll.

candidates.label: ChooseAction
candidates.comment: The act of expressing a preference or making a selection from a set of options. Also called select, pick, opt for, decide. Examples: Choosing a meal from a menu, choosing a candidate in an election, choosing a color for a car.

candidates.label: PlanAction
candidates.comment: PlanAction is an OrganizeAction that involves arranging the execution of an event, task, action, reservation, or plan for a future time. Also called scheduling, arranging, pre-arranging. Examples: planning a wedding, scheduling a meeting, arranging a trip itinerary, setting up a project timeline.

candidates.label: CreateAction
candidates.comment: A CreateAction is the act of deliberately producing, generating, or building a new result or entity by an agent. Also called production, generation, fabrication, construction. Examples: Writing a book, composing a song, building a house, designing a website.

candidates.label: OrganizeAction
candidates.comment: An OrganizeAction, as an Action, is the act of manipulating, administering, supervising, or controlling one or more objects. Also called arrange, manage, coordinate. Examples: organizing a conference, managing a project, arranging files on a computer. Distinct from CreateAction, which focuses on producing something new.

types.embedding_query_text: Competition: An event or contest in which people or teams compete against each other. Also called Tournament, Championship, Match, Game. Examples: World Cup, UEFA Super Cup, Club World Cup.

chosen_type.label: SportsEvent
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org SportsEvent class directly matches the OIE_TYPE 'Competition' and its definition, as all examples are major athletic competitions.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

types.embedding_query_text: Group: A number of people or things that are located, gathered, or classed together. Also called Team, Collective, Assembly, Body. Examples: Private investors, 211 member associations.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: While 'Group' is broad, 'Organization' is the best fit among candidates. '211 member associations' clearly refers to an organization, and 'Private investors' can represent a collective acting as an organization.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

types.embedding_query_text: Document: A piece of written, printed, or electronic matter that provides information or evidence or that serves as an official record. Also called Record, Report, File, Paper. Examples: Joint letter, letter of support.

chosen_type.label: TextDigitalDocument
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org TextDigitalDocument class is a specific and accurate fit for 'Document' when the examples are 'Joint letter' and 'letter of support', which are textual documents.

candidates.label: DigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an electronic file or document. Also called Electronic document, e-document, digital file, computer file. Examples: A PDF report, a Word document, a spreadsheet, an image file, an e-book. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: NoteDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A NoteDigitalDocument, as a DigitalDocument, is a file containing a note, primarily for the author's reference. Also called digital note, electronic memo, text note. Examples: a personal reminder in a digital format, a draft of an idea, a quick thought saved electronically. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is intended for public consumption.

candidates.label: TextDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A digital document primarily composed of textual content. Also called text file, digital document, e-document. Examples: a PDF report, a Word document, an e-book. Distinct from TextObject, which is a media object representing a text file, often for embedding or linking.

candidates.label: Manuscript
candidates.comment: A creative work, such as a book, document, or musical piece, written by hand rather than typed or printed. Also called handwritten document, original script, autograph. Examples: a medieval illuminated manuscript, an author's handwritten draft of a novel, a composer's original musical score.

candidates.label: SpreadsheetDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A digital document designed for organizing and analyzing data in rows and columns, typically containing formulas and charts. Also called spreadsheet file, data sheet, workbook, Excel file. Examples: a budget spreadsheet, a sales report in Google Sheets, a financial model in Microsoft Excel.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A particular day, month, or year, often specified in the text. Also called Day, Calendar date, Specific day. Examples: March next year, Thursday, Wednesday, 2027.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Date datatype is the most encompassing for 'a particular day, month, or year', covering 'March next year' and '2027'. While 'DayOfWeek' is specific for 'Thursday'/'Wednesday', Date can represent specific days within a calendar.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large town or urban area. Also called Metropolis, Town, Urban center. Examples: Salzburg.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org City class is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE 'City' and the example 'Salzburg'.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

candidates.label: ShoppingCenter
candidates.comment: A large retail complex containing multiple stores and businesses, often with shared parking. Also called mall, shopping mall, retail complex, plaza. Examples: 'Westfield Century City', 'Mall of America', 'The Grove'.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.embedding_query_text: Event: A happening or occurrence, especially one of importance. Also called Occurrence, Incident, Happening, Affair. Examples: FAI Board Meeting.

chosen_type.label: Event
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Event class is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE 'Event' and the example 'FAI Board Meeting'.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: EducationEvent
candidates.comment: An EducationEvent is an Event focused on learning or instruction. Also called educational activity, learning event, training session. Examples: A university lecture, a workshop on coding, a seminar on financial literacy, a school field trip.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

types.embedding_query_text: Time Period: A duration or span of time. Also called Period, Interval, Duration, Span. Examples: earlier this year, this week.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Duration class accurately represents a 'period of time', which aligns with the OIE_TYPE 'Time Period' and examples like 'earlier this year' and 'this week'.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

types.embedding_query_text: Concept: An abstract idea or general notion. Also called Idea, Notion, Principle, Abstract. Examples: Irish football, governance, transparency, meaningful consultation.

chosen_type.label: DefinedTerm
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org DefinedTerm class is the best fit for 'Concept', as it represents abstract ideas or general notions that can be formally defined, such as 'governance' or 'transparency'.

candidates.label: DefinedTerm
candidates.comment: An intangible entity representing a word, phrase, or acronym with a formal definition, often used in glossaries or classification schemes. Also called Glossary entry, vocabulary term, classification code, concept. Examples: "ISBN" (International Standard Book Number), "HTTP" (Hypertext Transfer Protocol), "Organic" (as a food label). Distinct from DefinedTermSet, which is a collection of such terms.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: Claim
candidates.comment: A specific, factually-oriented statement that can be reviewed for accuracy. Also called assertion, statement, proposition, contention. Examples: "The Earth is flat," "Coffee cures cancer," "This product is 100% organic." Distinct from ClaimReview, which is the review of a claim.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: Class
candidates.comment: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.

types.embedding_query_text: Role: The function or position that someone has in an organization, society, or in a particular situation. Also called Position, Capacity, Function, Office. Examples: FIFA President, FIFA Vice-president, CAF President, UEFA President.

chosen_type.label: OrganizationRole
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org OrganizationRole class is a more specific and accurate fit than the general 'Role', as all examples ('FIFA President', 'CAF President') are positions within organizations.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: OrganizationRole
candidates.comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.

candidates.label: EmployeeRole
candidates.comment: An EmployeeRole is an OrganizationRole describing the relationship of an individual as an employee within an organization. Also called job position, staff role, employment status. Examples: "Software Engineer" at Google, "Marketing Manager" at a startup, "Cashier" at a supermarket.

candidates.label: PerformanceRole
candidates.comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.

candidates.label: LinkRole
candidates.comment: A LinkRole is an intangible role representing a Web link, allowing for the specification of link relationships and other HTML link element details outside of HTML. Also called URL role, hyperlink descriptor, web link attribute. Examples: a link with 'linkRelationship' 'amphtml', a canonical URL link, a link to a related resource.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Country class is the closest concept to represent 'Nationality', as 'Swiss' refers to the country Switzerland.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: NLNonprofitType
candidates.comment: NLNonprofitType is an enumeration for specific non-profit organization types originating from the Netherlands. Also called Dutch non-profit type, Netherlands charity classification. Examples: ANBI (Algemeen Nut Beogende Instelling), SBBI (Sociaal Belang Behartigende Instelling). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a general enumeration for non-profit types.

candidates.label: DENonprofitType
candidates.comment: DENonprofitType is an enumeration representing specific types of non-profit organizations recognized under German fiscal code, article 52. Also called German non-profit classification, AO 52 non-profit. Examples: A German charitable foundation, a registered German association for public benefit.

candidates.label: ITNonprofitType
candidates.comment: ITNonprofitType is a nonprofit type enumeration specifically for non-profit organizations originating from Italy. Also called Italian non-profit category, Italy NPO type, Italian charity classification. Examples: 'ONLUS', 'APS', 'ODV' (specific Italian non-profit legal forms). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a more general enumeration of non-profit organization types.

candidates.label: RestrictedDiet
candidates.comment: A RestrictedDiet is an Enumeration representing a diet limited to certain foods or preparations due to cultural, religious, health, or lifestyle reasons. Also called special diet, dietary restriction. Examples: vegan diet, gluten-free diet, kosher diet, low-sodium diet.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org Quantity datatype is a direct match for the OIE_TYPE 'Quantity' and can represent a numerical value like '56' as a measurable amount.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: TypeAndQuantityNode
candidates.comment: A structured value indicating the quantity, unit of measurement, and business function of goods within a bundle offer. Also called quantity specification, offer item details, bundle component. Examples: "3 kg of apples for sale", "2 units of product X as a bonus", "1 liter of milk in a grocery bundle".

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".
